items.title: The AI cold war needs a nonalignment movement
Brexit Britain: Sunlit Uplands or a Toad in the Harrow?
items.description: Political change in Britain has dominated the headlines, with Keir Starmer’s resignation paving the way for Andy Burnham, as the country also marks ten years since the Brexit vote. Fresh peace talks between the US and Iran have begun amid continuing tensions and sharply different accounts of progress from both sides.

items.title: Palestinians grieve for a father-to-be shot by Israeli troops the day his son was born
items.description: Nayef Samaro, 25, was killed in an Israeli military raid on Nablus, in the occupied West Bank, as he prepared to meet his wife at the hospital for the birth of their first child.

items.title: In Viral Post, Russian Veteran Warns Putin Of Mutiny, Then Walks Back Threat
items.description: A veteran of Russia’s war against Ukraine sparked a stir with a viral video post, demanding a meeting with President Vladimir Putin and warning of a rebellion – before retracting the threat. The episode highlighted growing tensions in Russia over a war estimated to have killed half a million Russian soldiers.

items.title: Aid groups urge swift action to avert ‘atrocities’ in Sudan’s el-Obeid
items.description: The city is at risk of an 'imminent ground offensive' by the RSF paramilitary and its allies, 38 NGOs warn.

items.title: 4 IDF soldiers injured in Lebanon clash with Hezbollah gunman, ahead of another day of talks
items.description: Officer moderately hurt, 3 others lightly injured as gunman lobs grenade at forces; terror group chief says US-Iran deal a defeat for Israel; cabinet said to spar over war policy The post 4 IDF soldiers injured in Lebanon clash with Hezbollah gunman, ahead of another day of talks appeared first on The Times of Israel.

items.title: Sudan: Fears of atrocities as RSF surrounds key city
items.description: As Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces mass around the strategic city of el-Obeid, fears are growing of atrocities similar to those seen in Darfur's el-Fasher. Could sanctions still prevent bloodshed?

items.title: Ukraine's Donbas rear area, from Sloviansk to Kramatorsk, is under constant Russian pressure
items.description: 'Donbas: The War of Attrition' (1/2). Just a few kilometers from one of Ukraine's fiercest fronts, these two cities are under drone strikes that make residents' lives very difficult. Both civilians and soldiers fear the bombings will intensify.

items.title: Thousands trapped in southern Ukraine struggle to survive
items.description: Thousands of civilians trapped in frontline communities in southern Ukraine are facing a deepening humanitarian crisis as access to food, medical care and evacuation routes continues to shrink, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in the country, HMRRU, warned on Wednesday.

items.title: Trump asks Congress for billions for Iran war, after tension with Republicans
items.description: But the budget faces an uphill battle as the president spars with some members of his own party over the issue.

items.title: Yabloko Deputy Leader Jailed 7 Years for ‘War Fakes’
items.description: Maxim Kruglov, a former Moscow city councilman, was arrested in October over social media posts from April 2022 discussing civilian deaths following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

items.title: In High-Stakes Bluff, Putin Holds a Losing Hand
items.description: Ukraine’s recent battlefield successes do not bode well for the Kremlin leader. Thanks to Europe’s steady financial and military support for Kyiv, Russia is experiencing casualties unprecedented since World War II. Meanwhile, the US waivers in its historic transatlantic commitment.
